_meta.note: Real Indian policy instruments, summarised for screening only. Terms change; always verify the current notification on the official portal before relying on eligibility. No subsidy amounts are asserted.

schemes.name: Fly Ash Utilisation Notification
schemes.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change
schemes.relevance: Thermal plants must ensure full utilisation of ash, including legacy ash, and bear transport costs for eligible uses within a notified radius. That makes ash offtake cheap or free for cement, brick and road users.
verify: Current utilisation targets and penalty clauses
Transport-cost radius in the latest amendment
Whether the use is on the notified eligible-use list

schemes.name: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management & Transboundary Movement) Rules
schemes.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change / CPCB
schemes.relevance: Using listed wastes as a resource requires authorisation from the state pollution control board. CPCB publishes standard operating procedures for specific utilisation routes.
verify: Is a CPCB SOP published for this material–use pair?

schemes.name: Construction & Demolition Waste Management Rules
schemes.authority: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change
schemes.relevance: Creates obligations to process C&D waste and to procure recycled C&D products in public works. That gives recycled aggregate a policy-backed buyer.
verify: Whether the newer C&D rules notification applies in your state
Local-body procurement percentage for recycled products

schemes.name: Steel Scrap Recycling Policy
schemes.relevance: Sets a framework for scientific processing and recycling of ferrous residues. Useful for positioning mill-scale and slag recovery as policy-aligned practice.

schemes.name: Green Steel Taxonomy
schemes.relevance: Classifies steel by emissions intensity. Documented by-product utilisation supports a producer's sustainability disclosures and green-steel positioning.
verify: How by-product credits are treated in the emissions-intensity boundary

schemes.name: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (compliance mechanism)
schemes.authority: Ministry of Power / Bureau of Energy Efficiency
schemes.relevance: Obligated sectors such as cement and steel receive GHG-intensity targets. Lower clinker factor or lower ore use from by-products can help meet the target or generate tradeable certificates.
